text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Corporate leaders contacted by The Australian Financial Review have given the Howard Government a seven out of ten rating, but urge the Government to show more 'vision'. Business has been generally happy with the performance of the Government, except when cutbacks have hit companies, and also supports the Government's industrial relations reforms. Page 1.

Adelaide-based Normandy Mining executive chairman Robert de Crespigny says the company would be able to survive for four or five years if, in a worst-case scenario, the price of gold fell to US$100. The group, Australia's largest gold group, carries the largest number of forward sales in Australia and possibly the world. Page 1.

General Motors Holden chief executive Bill Hamel, who will retire this week after 20 years with the company, said the car maker will suffer a drop in profit for 1996 after its record 1995 result of A$260 million. Hamel suggested the drop in profit is due to a soft Australian car market and increased costs associated with a heavy investment program for its new Vectra model. Page 4.

Australasian Soft Drink Association chief executive Tony Gentile, a representative of industrial sugar users, is pushing the Federal Government not to give in the National Party backbenchers who are against a Cabinet decision to abolish the sugar tariff fom July. Page 5.

The completion of the A$610 million expansion of the massive Escondida mine in Chile in about two years will see BHP become the world's biggest producer of copper metal through the new low-cost Solvent Extraction-Electrowinning process. By 1999, up to a third of BHP's total copper output will be produced using the new technology. Page 23.

Amid speculation of a takeover bid, Country Road will this week issue section 261 notices to identify who is behind the recent buying of its shares. There are rumours that Coles Myer's largest shareholder, Soloman Lew, is behind the turnover of more than 1.3 million Country Road shares late last week. Page 24.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Talks to be held in Melbourne this week will effect the early development of the proposed A$7 billion Gorgon gas project off the West Australian coast. The talks are aimed at convincing Shell to take a stake in the nearby Chrysaor discovery, and corporate sources believes negotiations between energy giants Chevron, Texaco and Shell to restructure the ownership of Chrysaor are delicate. Page 17.

Ansett International last week applied to code-share with Air New Zealand on flights to Malaysia, a move that extends the partnership between the two airlines beyond their domestic and trans-Tasman routes. However, Malaysia would probably be the only intrnational route Ansett would share, given that Malaysia is one of only a handful of countries that have agreed with Australia to allow code-share agreements that include a third country. Page 17.

Australian Pharmaceutical Manufacturers Association chief executive Pat Clear yesterday the industry yesterday stepped up the industry's campaign to ensure the protection of the Factor (f) scheme by warning any cuts to the program would undermine Australi's depleted research and development base, and could hurt local drug companies. Page 17.

Press reports in New Zealand indicate at least two Australian life insurance companies, AMP Society and Tyndall Life, are competing to spend up to A$150 million to buy New Zealand's third largest life insurer, NZI Life. Other contenders include UK-based Pudential and guardian Assurance Groups, yet Australia's National Mutual was a late drop out. Page 19.

Primary Industries Minister John Anderson has warned the divided wheat industry that it must present a unified front on the issue of the future commercial structure of the Australian Wheat Board. Anderson said that without the unified front, the Government would impose a solution on the industry. Page 19.

National Australia Bank head Don Argus told an Institute of Chartered Accountants conference in Queensland that credit standards are slipping amid the battle for market share between Australian financial institutions, was in a way similar to the mid 1980s when banks ran up multi-billion dollar losses. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In a weekend address to Institute of Chartered Accountants, the head of National Australia Bank Don Argus warned that standards in the banking industry are falling, forcing an environment which could lead to a repeat of the bad debt crisis that consumed the sector in the 1980s. Page 35.

The Seven Network's Supreme Court bid to win control of Optus Vision will begin today, and is expected to be the most important two weeks in Australian pay-TV's short life. If Seven wins the court battle, fellow Optus Vision shareholders Optus Communicatons, US West and Publishing and Broadcasting will be out of the Australian pay-TV market. Page 35.

Following Wall Street's Dow Jones index finishing 4.24 points higher at 6931.62 on Friday, the Australian sharemarket should open on a stronger note this week. Australian investors will be relying on the swag of interim profit results which will be delivered this week. Page 37.

The Institute of Chartered Accountants has sent an 11 minute video to all members of the Coalition outlining its objections to the superannuation surcharge. This is a last ditch effort to oppose the charge, which will increase the tax payable on employerpaid super contributions by one percentage point for each A$1,000 of gross salary above A$70,000 a year, until the tax, normally 15 per cent of contributions, hits 30 per cent at a salary level of A$85,000. Page 37.

Prime Minister John Howard said at the weekend in an address to the Chinese Australia Forum that the Federal Government has pledged to deliver a major breakthrough for small business when it responds to an independent review of red tape in mid-March. Thereview was completed last year and looked into all facets of business regulation. Page 37.

A report by Professor Mark Armstrong and Ross Kelso of the Media and Telecommunications Policy Group at RMIT has found that consumers face high costs and the prospect of having to buy multiple set-top units to access on-line services such as the Internet,pay-TV and digital broadcasting. Page 38.
THE AGE

The head of the National Australia Bank, Don Argus, has warned that intense competition in the banking and credit sector is forcing a reduction in standards which could lead to a bad debt crisis similar to that which plagued the industry in the 1980s. Pag C1.

Shareholders of newspaper group Fairfax Holdings have voted against a proposal by Brierley Investments which aimed to lift its stake from 19.9 per cent to 25 per cent. This move means Brierley will have to increase its offer of A$2.82 a share if it wants o take out a the sought-after five per cent stake. Page C1.

Several international companies are believed to have shown interest in buying a strategic stake in the Federal Government's engineering and technology group, Australian Defence Industries. A 100 per cent sale of ADI is tipped to raise between A$200 million and A$300 million for the Commonwealth. Page C1.

Woolworths managing director Reg Clairs said yesterday the company should make a small profit within a year of the expansion of its wholesaling operations through Australian Independent Wholesalers Pty Ltd (AIW). Clairs stated on Business Sunday that resarch indicated that the number of independent retailers likely to come on board would enable Woolworths to do better than break even. Page C2.

Qantas Airways managing director James Strong said on yesterday's Business Sunday program that be believed the airline would return to paying fully franked dividends later this year. Strong said the company aim was to maintain the franking. Page C2.

Professor Mark Armstrong of the Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology says in his new book Interfacing on the On-Line World: Pay TV, Broadband Standards and Access that Australia may become too small a market for services such as the Internet, pay TV an digital broadcasting unless all three can be combined in a single household unit. Page C2.
